1	import {
2	  currentEntitlements,
3	  regeneratesUsedToday,
4	  recordGeneration,
5	  checkGeneration,
6	  type GenerationKind,
7	} from "@/lib/billing/entitlements";
8	import { QuotaExceededError } from "@/lib/billing/errors";
9	
10	// Re-exported so the generator's call sites keep importing their gate and its
11	// error from one place. The class itself lives in `lib/billing/errors`, which
12	// carries no `server-only` — tests and any future client-side display of the
13	// remaining allowance must be able to reference it.
14	export { QuotaExceededError } from "@/lib/billing/errors";
15	
16	/**
17	 * What the GATE needs to know.
18	 *
19	 * The reroll allowance is a single daily pool across all occasions, so the gate
20	 * needs only the date. `occasion` rides along for the ledger, and is optional
21	 * because the styled action resolves its occasion only AFTER this gate —
22	 * deliberately, so a free user is turned away before we pay for a forecast
23	 * fetch they will never see.
24	 */
25	export type GenerationCheckRequest = {
26	  kind: GenerationKind;
27	  /** Recorded, not used by the check. */
28	  occasion?: string;
29	  /** The user's LOCAL date — never the server's. */
30	  today: string;
31	};
32	
33	/** What the LEDGER needs. `generation_events.occasion` is NOT NULL. */
34	export type GenerationRequest = GenerationCheckRequest & { occasion: string };
35	
36	/**
37	 * The single gate every real generation passes through.
38	 *
39	 * It was written as a deliberate no-op so that adding a paid tier later would be
40	 * a change to THIS file rather than surgery across the generate action. This is
41	 * that change: the decision now lives in `lib/billing`, and this stays the one
42	 * call site the generator knows about.
43	 *
44	 * The three kinds are metered differently (docs/MONETISATION.md §2):
45	 *   drop       — always free, on every tier. The daily drop is never rationed.
46	 *   regenerate — free gets three a day, pooled across every occasion.
47	 *   styled     — Pro only.
48	 */
49	export async function assertCanGenerate(
50	  _userId: string,
51	  req: GenerationCheckRequest,
52	): Promise<void> {
53	  const e = await currentEntitlements();
54	
55	  // Only a reroll needs the counter, so drops and styled looks skip the query
56	  // rather than paying for an answer that cannot change the outcome.
57	  const regeneratesUsed =
58	    req.kind === "regenerate" ? await regeneratesUsedToday(req.today) : 0;
59	
60	  const check = checkGeneration(e, { kind: req.kind, regeneratesUsed });
61	  if (!check.allowed) throw new QuotaExceededError(check.reason);
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Record a generation that actually happened.
66	 *
67	 * Deliberately separate from the check, and called only AFTER the model request
68	 * succeeds: a failed generation costs the user nothing, so charging for one
69	 * would be charging for our own error.
70	 */
71	export async function noteGeneration(userId: string, req: GenerationRequest): Promise<void> {
72	  await recordGeneration(userId, req.occasion, req.today, req.kind);
73	}

-- Which tier a user is on. A plain text column with a check constraint rather
-- than an enum type: adding a tier later ('trialing', when the trial model is
-- decided) is then an ALTER of the constraint, not a type migration with a
-- rewrite.
--
-- This is the ONLY source of tier truth. Nothing derives a tier from a Stripe
-- webhook payload at read time; billing's job will be to write this column.
alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists tier text not null default 'free'
  check (tier in ('free', 'pro'));

-- `profiles` carries a self-update RLS policy, so without this a user could run
-- `update profiles set tier = 'pro'` from the browser with the anon key and
-- grant themselves the paid tier. RLS decides WHICH ROWS you may touch; it does
-- not decide which COLUMNS, so the policy alone cannot express "you own this row
-- but not this field".
--
-- Reads are unaffected (the own-row select policy still applies), and the local
-- dev override is an env var (FITCHECK_FORCE_TIER), not this column, so nothing
-- in development depends on writing it. Billing will write it as service_role.
revoke update (tier) on public.profiles from authenticated;

-- Every real AI generation, recorded.
--
-- The `outfits` rows CANNOT serve as this counter, for two independent reasons:
--
--   1. A regenerate REPLACES the day's rows for an occasion (saveDailyLooks is
--      delete-then-insert), so the act of regenerating erases its own evidence.
--      Counting rows afterwards cannot tell a first drop from a fifth.
--   2. saveDailyLooks writes one row per LOOK, three per generation, so a row
--      count reports 3 after a single drop.
--
-- This ledger is append-only and is the only thing the meter reads.
create table if not exists public.generation_events (
  id           uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id      uuid not null references public.profiles(id) on delete cascade,
  occasion     text not null,
  generated_on date not null,          -- the user's LOCAL date, as with outfits
  -- Three kinds, not a boolean. "Style an outfit with this" (PR #22) is neither
  -- the day's free drop for an occasion nor a regenerate of one: recording it as
  -- a drop would mark that occasion as already dropped, and recording it as a
  -- regenerate would make styling eat the regenerate allowance.
  kind         text not null check (kind in ('drop', 'regenerate', 'styled')),
  created_at   timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.generation_events enable row level security;

create policy generation_events_own on public.generation_events
  for all
  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);

-- The meter's hot path: "what has this user spent on their local today?"
create index if not exists generation_events_user_day_idx
  on public.generation_events (user_id, generated_on);

grant select, insert on public.generation_events to authenticated;

content.content:
1	export type Tier = "free" | "pro";
2	
3	/** The three things that spend a model request. See docs/MONETISATION.md §2. */
4	export type GenerationKind = "drop" | "regenerate" | "styled";
5	
6	export type Entitlements = {
7	  tier: Tier;
8	  /**
9	   * Rerolls per DAY, across all occasions. null = unlimited.
10	   *
11	   * Global rather than per-occasion (user decision, 2026-08-05). Most people
12	   * care about one occasion on a given day, so a per-occasion allowance is
13	   * strictest exactly where attention goes and generous where nobody is
14	   * looking: you could be refused a second Work reroll while holding an unused
15	   * Evening one you never wanted.
16	   *
17	   * The usual objection to a global pool — that it can block an occasion you
18	   * have not opened yet — does not apply here, because a drop is free on every
19	   * tier. Tapping a new occasion is always a drop, so the pool only ever meters
20	   * rerolls.
21	   */
22	  regeneratesPerDay: number | null;
23	  /**
24	   * How many pieces a closet may hold. null = unlimited.
25	   *
26	   * Counts UNARCHIVED items only. Archiving is the user's way to make room —
27	   * there is no delete path in the product, so counting archived pieces would
28	   * strand a user at the cap with no way out. It also matches what the number
29	   * claims: an archived piece is not in your closet.
30	   *
31	   * 50 is deliberately well clear of the ~20-30 range where combo coverage
32	   * thins (PR #15 measured a 21-item closet at 21 combos in winter against 48
33	   * in summer), so the free tier never experiences a starved stylist — it
34	   * experiences a full one, with a ceiling.
35	   */
36	  closetItems: number | null;
37	  /** "Style an outfit with this" — Pro #2. */
38	  styledLooks: boolean;
39	  savedOutfits: number | null;
40	  /** The Wear Stats SCREEN. The per-item tile on item detail is free. */
41	  analytics: boolean;
42	  gapAnalysis: boolean;
43	  packingMode: boolean;
44	};
45	
46	/**
47	 * The tiers, as data. See docs/MONETISATION.md for the reasoning — in short:
48	 * meter what costs us money, sell what compounds, and never gate the daily
49	 * drop, the share card, or the closet.
50	 *
51	 * The free ceiling is four occasion drops plus three rerolls = 7 generations a
52	 * day, about $0.63/month at $0.003 each and nearer $0.20 in realistic use.
53	 * **The ceiling is the point** — a free tier needs a worst case you can
54	 * survive, and this one cannot be raised by adding clothes.
55	 */
56	export const FREE: Entitlements = {
57	  tier: "free",
58	  regeneratesPerDay: 3,
59	  closetItems: 50,
60	  styledLooks: false,
61	  savedOutfits: 10,
62	  analytics: false,
63	  gapAnalysis: false,
64	  packingMode: false,
65	};
66	
67	export const PRO: Entitlements = {
68	  tier: "pro",
69	  regeneratesPerDay: null,
70	  closetItems: null,
71	  styledLooks: true,
72	  savedOutfits: null,
73	  analytics: true,
74	  gapAnalysis: true,
75	  packingMode: true,
76	};
77	
78	// The pure functions live HERE, not in entitlements.ts, so tests can import them
79	// without dragging in `server-only` (which does not resolve under jsdom).
80	// entitlements.ts re-exports them for app code.
81	
82	/** Unknown input resolves to free: capabilities fail CLOSED. */
83	export function entitlementsFor(tier: unknown): Entitlements {
84	  return tier === "pro" ? PRO : FREE;
85	}
86	
87	export type GenerationCheck = {
88	  allowed: boolean;
89	  /** null = unlimited. Only meaningful for a metered kind. */
90	  remaining: number | null;
91	  reason?: string;
92	};
93	
94	/**
95	 * May this user spend a model request right now?
96	 *
97	 * `regeneratesUsed` is the user's total reroll count for their local today,
98	 * across every occasion.
99	 *
100	 * A drop is never metered on any tier: MONETISATION §1 and Decision 4 both say
101	 * the daily drop is the product, and rationing it is how nobody discovers the
102	 * magic. That is also what makes a global reroll pool safe — a user can always
103	 * open any occasion, so the pool can never strand them.
104	 */
105	export function checkGeneration(
106	  e: Entitlements,
107	  input: { kind: GenerationKind; regeneratesUsed: number },
108	): GenerationCheck {
109	  if (input.kind === "drop") return { allowed: true, remaining: null };
110	
111	  if (input.kind === "styled") {
112	    return e.styledLooks
113	      ? { allowed: true, remaining: null }
114	      : {
115	          allowed: false,
116	          remaining: 0,
117	          reason: "Building a look around a piece is a Pro feature.",
118	        };
119	  }
120	
121	  if (e.regeneratesPerDay == null) return { allowed: true, remaining: null };
122	  const remaining = Math.max(0, e.regeneratesPerDay - input.regeneratesUsed);
123	  return remaining > 0
124	    ? { allowed: true, remaining }
125	    : {
126	        allowed: false,
127	        remaining: 0,
128	        reason: `That's your ${e.regeneratesPerDay} rerolls for today. Pro rerolls without limit.`,
129	      };
130	}
131	
132	/**
133	 * May this user add another piece?
134	 *
135	 * `held` is the number of UNARCHIVED pieces already in the closet — archiving
136	 * is how a free user makes room, since nothing in the product deletes an item.
137	 */
138	export function checkCloset(e: Entitlements, held: number): GenerationCheck {
139	  if (e.closetItems == null) return { allowed: true, remaining: null };
140	  const remaining = Math.max(0, e.closetItems - held);
141	  return remaining > 0
142	    ? { allowed: true, remaining }
143	    : {
144	        allowed: false,
145	        remaining: 0,
146	        reason: `A free closet holds ${e.closetItems} pieces. Pro is unlimited — or archive something you no longer wear.`,
147	      };
148	}

content.text:
Based on my investigation of the diff and the surrounding context (RLS policies, callers of the changed functions), I've traced:

1. **`assertCanUpload()` removal of `.eq("user_id", user.id)`** — The query now relies purely on RLS. Verified: `items` table has `enable row level security` with policy `using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)`. Caller `uploadAndTag` still authenticates before calling. Safe.
